name: Lysozyme
aliases: E1105, INS 1105, lysozyme, lysozyme hydrochloride, muramidase
what_is: An enzyme/protein used as a food additive. The EU specification for E1105 defines lysozyme as a polypeptide obtained from hen egg white, usually supplied as the hydrochloride.
why_botia: BOTIA flags E1105 because its declared additive name also carries source information relevant to the animal-origin layer. EU rules specifically addressed lysozyme from hen egg white and its labelling in food uses such as certain beers.
can_1: Detect E1105, lysozyme, lysozyme hydrochloride and muramidase when declared.
can_2: Show the animal-origin and E-number context and explain the egg-white origin defined in the EU additive specification.
cannot_1: Determine the concentration or remaining enzymatic activity from the ingredient list.
cannot_2: Assume that an unlabeled food contains lysozyme or infer a different source when the label gives no such information.

sources.label: Commission Regulation (EU) No 231/2012 — E1105 Lysozyme specification
